pr_title: Include `numSelectedRepos` in JSON output of `gh secret list`
pr_body:
This PR fixes unset/zero `numSelectedRepos` value within the JSON exported output of `gh secret list`, thanks to @andyfeller investigation and guidance.

Fixes #8679 

## Notes

In this PR, we explicitly check for the `numSelectedRepos` field in the `--json` argument, if any. The reason is to keep the current behavior as intact as possible, and also to avoid unnecessary API requests (which are per secret, to fetch selected repos).
pr_comments: Sorry for the force-push, my bad. I really didn't want to push another commit just to revert the ordering/grouping of imports.

@andyfeller I've just pushed some changes to improve the implementation and tests, while keeping the current presentation behavior the same (i.e., as seen by the end users):

1. We now only populate the `numSelectedRepos` field, in these cases:
   1. The `gh secret list` command is run in the TTY mode without the `--json <fields>` option, in which case the output is a table showing the number of selected repositories.
   2. The `gh secret list` command is run with `--json <fields>` option, and `numSelectedRepos` **is** among the selected fields. In this case, TTY mode is irrelevant.
   
   In other cases, the value of the `numSelectedRepos` will not be present in the output and therefore we should avoid further API requests (to fetch the selected repositories).
   
2. I added a new test function to assert the above behavior. To keep the test simple, I just relied on the number of requests made. Alternatives were to intercept the call to the `Exporter.Write` method (to check `NumSelectedRepos` is actually set to a non-zero value), or even export-then-mock the internal `populateSelectedRepositoryInformation` method (which loops through the secrets and fetches the number of selected repos), but neither were as simple as the request counting approach.

issue_context.title: Exporting `gh secret list` should always provide number of selected repositories
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When using `gh secret list -o <org> --json 'name,numSelectedRepos'` and sending the output to a file or to another process, the integers from `numSelectedRepos` are set to 0. However if the standard output is the interactive terminal, then the values are correct

gh version: 2.43.1, happens all the way back to 2.36.0 when `--json` option appeared.

I have only seen this behavior with `gh secret list`, I could not reproduce it with `gh issue -R zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr list --json 'number' | cat -` for instance.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a github organisation `dummyOrg`
2. Create at least one repository inside `dummyOrg`
3. Create a secret at the organisation level and share that secret with the repository created in previous step
4. List secret at organisation level with json formatting: `gh secret list -o dummyOrg --json 'name,numSelectedRepos' | cat -`
5. the `numSelectedRepos` field is set to zero instead of 1.

### Expected vs actual behavior

I am expecting the `numSelectedRepos` field to have a consistent value when piping the output of `gh secret list` command or sending it to the terminal

### Logs

#### Sending output to terminal (expected behavior)
```bash
gh secret list -o dummyOrg --json 'name,numSelectedRepos'
[
  {
    "name": "MYSECRET",
    "numSelectedRepos": 1
  }
]
```

#### Sending output to another process (unexpected behavior)
```shell
gh secret list -o dummyOrg --json 'name,numSelectedRepos' | cat -
[{"name":"MYSECRET","numSelectedRepos":0}]
```
The `numSelectedRepos` has been converted to 0, the same unexpected behavior occurs with `jq` instead of `cat -` or sending the output to a file (` > file`)
comments:
@nvincent-vossloh : thank you for opening up this issue! 🙇 

After digging into the code a bit, I think I know where this is happening, which dates back to the origin of the command in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/4714:

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8948ee8c3beaf432676061aaaf481d2f41039483/pkg/cmd/secret/list/list.go#L117-L141

The code currently uses whether a TTY to show selected repository information or not.  I'm going to follow up regarding the concern and if there are any issues with relaxing that requirement. 👍 

### Update

**TLDR: We could relax this requirement, but it will increase API requests used.  Additionally, it appears `gh secret list` will only pull up to 100 secrets.**

Once secrets are retrieved, secondary enrichment of secrets will attempt to add number of repositories selected if relevant and depending on TTY.  Depending on whether you are using a PAT versus a GitHub App installation access token, that will just quicken the request per hour used.

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8948ee8c3beaf432676061aaaf481d2f41039483/pkg/cmd/secret/list/list.go#L276-L291

Lastly, it appears `gh secret list` is hard coded to pull a single 100 page of secrets from the API.  In the case of [limits of GitHub Actions secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions#limits-for-secrets), an organization can have up to 1,000.

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8948ee8c3beaf432676061aaaf481d2f41039483/pkg/cmd/secret/list/list.go#L258-L274
@andyfeller I just submitted a PR to fix this. Thanks for the hint.

> Lastly, it appears gh secret list is hard coded to pull a single 100 page of secrets from the API. In the case of [limits of GitHub Actions secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions#limits-for-secrets), an organization can have up to 1,000.

@andyfeller But that happens in a loop, so it'll fetch all secrets, right? Or I'm missing something?

review_comments:
**What level of testing do you think is appropriate when `numSelectedRepos` is not included in the fields to export?**

I'll admit this specific feature is weird from a testing perspective because we're still outputting `numSelectedRepos` even if we aren't retrieving the data.  So, it seems like there should be tests that mirror this but ensure the field is zeroed out unless it is provided as a field to export.

Good question, and I missed testing for it. I think I should add a couple of more tests to ensure we're handling both kind of cases (i.e., with or without `numSelectedRepos`). We already have the ones that **include** the `numSelectedRepos` field. I need to add the other half. I'll push another commit with the new test cases and will ask for review again.

I think it's not weird, because if `numSelectedRepos` was not there in the `--json` argument, then we won't print it out, so no weird zeros.
